questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Bethe-Weizsäcker semi-empirical mass formula, the asymmetry energy term is proportional to:
questions.explanationEn: The Pauli exclusion principle causes an energy penalty when $N \neq Z$, giving the asymmetry term $-a_a \frac{(A - 2Z)^2}{A} = -a_a \frac{(N - Z)^2}{A}$ in the binding energy.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following nuclei is doubly magic?
questions.explanationEn: The nuclear magic numbers are $2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126$. In $^{40}_{20}\text{Ca}$, both $Z = 20$ and $N = 20$ are magic numbers, making it doubly magic.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: The ratio of the nuclear radius of $^{216}\text{Po}$ to that of $^{27}\text{Al}$ is approximately:
questions.explanationEn: Using the empirical nuclear radius relation $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, the ratio is $R_1/R_2 = (216/27)^{1/3} = 8^{1/3} = 2$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: The quark content of a $K^+$ meson (charge $Q = +1$, strangeness $S = +1$) is:
questions.explanationEn: An up quark $u$ ($Q = +2/3, S = 0$) paired with an anti-strange quark $\bar{s}$ ($Q = +1/3, S = +1$) yields $Q = +1$ and $S = +1$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: The intrinsic parity of a meson ($q\bar{q}$ bound state) with orbital angular momentum $L$ is:
questions.explanationEn: A quark and antiquark have opposite intrinsic parities ($P_q P_{\bar{q}} = -1$). Including the spatial parity $(-1)^L$ gives total parity $P = -(-1)^L = (-1)^{L+1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: The strong spin-orbit interaction term $V_{SO}(r)\,\mathbf{L}\cdot\mathbf{S}$ in the nuclear shell model splits a level of orbital angular momentum $l$ ($l > 0$) such that:
optionsEn: The $j = l + \frac{1}{2}$ state lies lower in energy than the $j = l - \frac{1}{2}$ state
The $j = l - \frac{1}{2}$ state lies lower in energy than the $j = l + \frac{1}{2}$ state
questions.explanationEn: In nuclei, the spin-orbit potential is attractive for aligned spin and orbit ($V_{SO} < 0$), so $j = l + 1/2$ is lowered in energy relative to $j = l - 1/2$, opposite to atomic fine structure.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: The cross-section for absorption of very slow (thermal) neutrons by most nuclei away from resonances follows the $1/v$ law, meaning $\sigma_a$ is proportional to:
questions.explanationEn: Since neutron kinetic energy $E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \implies v \propto E^{1/2}$, the $1/v$ absorption law gives $\sigma_a \propto 1/v \propto E^{-1/2}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about the deuteron ($^2\text{H}$) are CORRECT?
optionsEn: Its binding energy is approximately $2.22\text{ MeV}$
Its magnetic dipole moment is exactly equal to the sum $\mu_p + \mu_n$
Its total isospin in the ground state is $I = 0$
It has no bound excited states
questions.explanationEn: The deuteron is weakly bound ($B \approx 2.22\text{ MeV}$) with no bound excited states and has $I=0$ ($^3S_1$ + $4\%$ $^3D_1$). Because of the $D$-state admixture, $\mu_d \approx 0.857\,\mu_N$ differs slightly from $\mu_p + \mu_n \approx 0.880\,\mu_N$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In the decay chain $^{238}_{92}\text{U} \to {}^{206}_{82}\text{Pb}$, the total number of $\beta^-$-particles emitted is ________. (in integer)
questions.explanationEn: With $N_\alpha = 8$, the atomic number drops by $2 \times 8 = 16$ from $\alpha$-decays, so $92 - 16 + N_{\beta^-} = 82 \implies N_{\beta^-} = 6$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: The hypercharge $Y = B + S$ of the $\Xi^0$ baryon (quark content $uss$) is ________. (in integer)
questions.explanationEn: For $\Xi^0$ ($uss$), baryon number $B = 1$ and strangeness $S = -2$ (two $s$ quarks). Hence $Y = B + S = 1 - 2 = -1$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: For a nucleus with a single unpaired proton in the $1d_{5/2}$ orbital ($j = l + \frac{1}{2}$, $g_l = 1$, $g_s = 5.586$), the Schmidt value of its nuclear magnetic dipole moment (in units of $\mu_N$) is approximately:
questions.explanationEn: For $j = l + 1/2$, the Schmidt formula is $\mu = \left(j - \frac{1}{2}\right)g_l + \frac{1}{2}g_s$. With $j=5/2, g_l=1, g_s=5.586$, $\mu = 2(1) + 2.793 = 4.793\,\mu_N \approx 4.79\,\mu_N$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In the constituent quark model assuming equal constituent masses for $u$ and $d$ quarks ($m_u = m_d$), the ratio of the magnetic moment of the neutron to that of the proton, $\mu_n / \mu_p$, is predicted to be:
questions.explanationEn: In $SU(6)$, $\mu_p = \frac{4}{3}\mu_u - \frac{1}{3}\mu_d$ and $\mu_n = \frac{4}{3}\mu_d - \frac{1}{3}\mu_u$. Since $q_u = +2/3$ and $q_d = -1/3$, $\mu_u = -2\mu_d$, giving $\mu_p = -3\mu_d$ and $\mu_n = 2\mu_d$, so $\mu_n / \mu_p = -2/3$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A thermal neutron is captured by $^{10}\text{B}$ to produce $^7\text{Li} + \alpha$. If the masses are $m(^{10}\text{B}) = 10.0129\text{ u}$, $m_n = 1.0087\text{ u}$, $m(^7\text{Li}) = 7.0160\text{ u}$, and $m(\alpha) = 4.0026\text{ u}$ (with $1\text{ u} \cdot c^2 = 931.5\text{ MeV}$), the $Q$-value of the reaction is approximately:

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the strong reaction $p + n \to d + \pi^0$ compared to $p + p \to d + \pi^+$. Using isospin invariance, the ratio of their cross-sections $\frac{\sigma(p + p \to d + \pi^+)}{\sigma(p + n \to d + \pi^0)}$ at the same center-of-mass energy is:
questions.explanationEn: The deuteron has $I=0$ and the pion has $I=1$, so the final state is pure $I=1$. Initial $pp$ is pure $|1, +1\rangle$, whereas $pn = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|1,0\rangle + |0,0\rangle)$ has only $\frac{1}{2}$ probability of being in $I=1$. Thus the cross-section ratio is $1 / (1/2) = 2$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about collective excitations of even-even nuclei are CORRECT?
optionsEn: Rotational bands are prominently observed in nuclei far from closed shells
Magic nuclei exhibit large permanent quadrupole deformations
For a pure harmonic quadrupole vibrational spectrum, the ratio $E(4^+)/E(2^+) = 2.0$
For a pure rotational band ($K=0$), the ratio $E(4^+)/E(2^+) = 10/3 \approx 3.33$
questions.explanationEn: Rotational bands give $E_4/E_2 = 10/3$ and occur far from closed shells; harmonic quadrupole vibrators have $E_4/E_2 = 2$ (two-phonon triplet $0^+, 2^+, 4^+$). Magic nuclei are spherical with zero permanent deformation.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following nuclear $\beta$-decay transitions are ALLOWED?
questions.explanationEn: Allowed $\beta$-transitions satisfy $\Delta J = 0, \pm 1$ and no parity change ($\Delta \pi = \text{no}$). Thus $0^+\to 0^+$ (Fermi), $0^+\to 1^+$ (Gamow-Teller), and $\frac{1}{2}^+\to\frac{1}{2}^+$ (mixed) are allowed, while $0^+\to 2^+$ has $\Delta J = 2$ (second forbidden).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Using the pairing term $\delta = \frac{12}{\sqrt{A}}\text{ MeV}$ in the semi-empirical mass formula, the energy difference between the even-even parabola and the odd-odd parabola for isobars of mass number $A = 100$ (in $\text{MeV}$) is ________. (rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: The even-even nuclei are shifted down in mass by $\delta$ and odd-odd nuclei are shifted up by $\delta$, so the vertical separation between the two mass parabolas is $2\delta = \frac{24}{\sqrt{100}} = 2.4\text{ MeV}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A radioactive isotope $X$ is produced at a constant rate of $10^6\text{ nuclei/s}$ in a reactor and decays with a decay constant $\lambda = 0.01\text{ s}^{-1}$. The activity of $X$ (in units of $10^5\text{ Bq}$) after $100\text{ s}$ from the start of irradiation is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: Activity builds up as $A(t) = R(1 - e^{-\lambda t})$. Here $\lambda t = 0.01 \times 100 = 1$, so $A(100) = 10^6(1 - e^{-1}) = 10^6(1 - 0.3679) = 6.321 \times 10^5\text{ Bq} \approx 6.32 \times 10^5\text{ Bq}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A $K^0$ meson (mass $498\text{ MeV}/c^2$) decays at rest into two pions $\pi^+ + \pi^-$ (each of mass $140\text{ MeV}/c^2$). The momentum of each pion (in $\text{MeV}/c$) is ________. (rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: Each pion gets energy $E_\pi = M_K / 2 = 249\text{ MeV}$. Momentum $p = \sqrt{E_\pi^2 - m_\pi^2} = \sqrt{249^2 - 140^2} = \sqrt{62001 - 19600} = \sqrt{42401} = 205.92\text{ MeV}/c \approx 205.9\text{ MeV}/c$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In the $\beta^-$-decay of $^{32}_{15}\text{P} \to {}^{32}_{16}\text{S} + e^- + \bar{\nu}_e$, the atomic mass difference is $M(^{32}\text{P}) - M(^{32}\text{S}) = 0.001836\text{ u}$. Using $1\text{ u}\cdot c^2 = 931.5\text{ MeV}$, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electron (in $\text{MeV}$) is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: For $\beta^-$-decay, $Q = [M(^{32}\text{P}) - M(^{32}\text{S})]c^2 = 0.001836 \times 931.5 = 1.7102\text{ MeV} \approx 1.71\text{ MeV}$.
